model_output.summary: Your progression from vehicle mechanic to platoon sergeant connects hands-on maintenance with leadership across supply and fuel. The resume describes supervisor-level responsibilities, including personnel evaluations, equipment accountability and a parts budget. Keeping 95% of vehicles mission-capable during the Poland deployment adds a useful operational result in a distinct setting. The remaining question is how your field logistics work translates into civilian supply chain tasks, which could affect how easily a reviewer maps it to a supervisor opening.
strengths: Accountability for $14M of vehicles, tools and equipment, with zero losses on three annual inventories, makes the inventory responsibility concrete.
Supervising 14 mechanics maintaining 62 wheeled vehicles shows the size of the shop and the fleet it supported.
Counseling and evaluating 6 direct-report sergeants, 4 of whom were promoted, shows a specific people-management responsibility alongside their subsequent progression.
gaps: The field-exercise bullet names the battalion and duration but not the supplies or services involved, making the logistics work less portable to civilian terminology.
The parts budget has an annual amount but does not explain which spending or ordering decisions you could make.
The training of 9 junior mechanics does not describe what you taught, so the technical development work is difficult to distinguish from general supervision.
